Before reporting a problem

Keep the details needed to troubleshoot

  1. Note the device, operating system version and cameraInclude the camera make and model shown in LensPin.
  2. Describe the location sourceSay whether the run used iPhone photos, another GPS camera’s photos, GPX, or an Apple Health workout route—and whether a clock offset was applied.
  3. Keep the completion counts or failure reasonAdded, failed, skipped, and album warnings describe different outcomes.
Protect private data.

Do not send a full photo library, private GPX route, or precise home coordinates when a filename, time gap, status label, and redacted screenshot are enough.

Troubleshoot photo locations

Missing GPS, wrong locations or photos absent from the map

LensPin FAQ

Which cameras are supported?

Photos from DSLR, mirrorless, compact and action cameras such as GoPro and Insta360 can be matched once they are in Apple Photos. LensPin needs readable capture-time and camera information. See supported formats for file limits.

Where do the locations come from?

Four sources: geotagged iPhone photos from the same trip; geotagged photos from other GPS-equipped cameras; GPX tracks; Apple Health workout routes.

Can I add locations to videos?

Yes. You can choose to include videos already in Apple Photos. The first 100 successful location additions are free, with a shared allowance for photos and videos. LensPin does not export GPS into video files.

What is the difference between the Mac and iPhone versions?

Both match capture times with geotagged reference photos or GPX tracks and save approved locations to the Photos library. On iPhone and iPad, you can also read Apple Health workout routes directly.

What if my camera clock or time zone was wrong?

Preview a camera clock offset to check the match without changing capture dates. Time-zone display options let you choose how times appear. Review the suggested places before saving.

How do I undo a wrong location?

Open the photo or video in the LensPin album and choose Remove Location. This removes its current Photos-library location. You can also adjust or remove a location in Apple Photos. It does not change GPS in the original file.
